uncited: - **Spatial Index (Implicit):** The method relies on the assumption that nearby pixels in 2D image space correspond to nearby 3D points.
**Same-View Candidate Generation:** For each query point $\mathbf{p}_q$ in the current view, project it to 2D pixel coordinates $(u, v)$.
Define a square window of size $(2r_s + 1) \times (2r_s + 1)$ centered at $(u, v)$.
Project the 3D query point $\mathbf{p}_q$ into the 2D image plane of view $v'$ using $\mathbf{K}_{v'}$ and $\mathbf{T}_{v'}$.
**Neighbor Selection:** Compute the 3D Euclidean distance between $\mathbf{p}_q$ and every point in $\mathcal{C}$.
- **Degenerate Input:** If $N$ is small or points are sparse, the candidate set may be empty.
It addresses the computational bottleneck of global kNN search in high-resolution point clouds.
